"''If I may say so, Your Majesty, the Chancellor has little real power. He is mired by baseless accusations of corruption. The bureaucrats are in charge now.|Padmé Amidala and Sheev Palpatine|}} '''Finis Valorum''' was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] [[Politics|politician]] from [[House Valorum]] who served as the penultimate [[Supreme Chancellor]] of the [[Galactic Republic]]. His chancellorship was hampered by corruption and bureaucracy in the [[Galactic Senate]], which he was unable to bring under control. Toward the end of his administration, Valorum attempted to resolve the [[Trade Federation]]'s [[Invasion of Naboo]], to little effect. As a result of government inaction, the [[Queen]], [[Padmé Amidala Naberrie|Padmé Amidala]], called for a [[Vote of No Confidence]] in his leadership. The Senate scheduled an [[Supreme Chancellor election, 32 BBY|election]] for a new Chancellor, and he was replaced by [[Senator]] [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine]] of Naboo; however, Palpatine was secretly Darth Sidious, the [[Dark Lord of the Sith]], and had orchestrated the Naboo Crisis to become Supreme Chancellor and, ultimately, [[Proclamation of the New Order|transform]] the Republic into the [[Galactic Empire]]. During the [[Clone Wars]], over ten [[Standard year|years]] after his political downfall, Valorum assisted the [[Jedi Order]] as they investigated the circumstances surrounding the [[death]] of [[Jedi Master]] [[Sifo-Dyas]] who, during the chancellor’s administration, had been sent on a [[Mission to Oba Diah (Sifo-Dyas)|mission]] to resolve a dispute with the [[spice]] dealers known as the [[Pyke Syndicate]]. The Jedi learned Sifo-Dyas had been killed during the mission by the Syndicate at the behest of the [[Sith]]; the dark lords had desired control of the [[Grand Army of the Republic|clone army]] he had secretly commissioned for the Republic. Much later, during the [[Imperial Era]], the Empire remembered the former chancellor as a weak, ineffectual leader who had done little to improve galactic order, while in contrast, some Coruscanti continued to have fond memories of their former head of state. ==Biography== ===Early career and chancellery=== Finis Valorum was [[Reproduction|born]] into the influential [[House Valorum]] on [[Coruscant]], the [[capital]] of the [[Galactic Republic]], and was a descendant of the Republic's [[Tarsus Valorum|first Supreme Chancellor]]. For his entire life, he planned to ascend to the [[Office of the Chancellor]].''[[Star Wars Character Encyclopedia: Updated and Expanded]]'' He entered into [[Politics|political]] life and became a civil servant within the Galactic Republic, where House Valorum held much prestige and influence. At some point early in his political career, he served as an [[administrator]] to [[Supreme Chancellor]] [[Skor Kalpana]], and with the chancellor, [[Senator]] [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine]] of [[Naboo]], and other dignitaries, Valorum attended the commencement and commissioning ceremonies at the [[Sullust Sector Spacefarers Academy]]. He was himself elected to the chancellery by the [[Galactic Senate]] in [[40 BBY]].''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the flashback section of [[Tarkin (novel)|''Tarkin'']] in which it is mentioned that Finis Valorum had been re-elected Chancellor to [[36 BBY]]. As ''[[Star Wars Propaganda: A History of Persuasive Art in the Galaxy]]'' establishes that the [[Galactic Republic]] Supreme Chancellors served four-[[Standard year|year]] terms, Valorum must have served as Chancellor beginning in [[40 BBY]]. Furthermore, ''Timelines'' dates his [[Vote of No Confidence|removal from office]] to [[32 BBY]]. During his administration, his political power became hampered by the massive bureaucracies of the government, and he became mired in accusations of corrupt conduct. At some point before the [[Invasion of Naboo]], the chancellor dispatched Jedi Master [[Mace Windu]] to [[Oosalon]] so he could free several kidnapped Jedi [[Padawan]]s from [[Guattako]] the Grim and end the threat there once and for all, as the fearless [[warlord]] was planning to continue with his pursuit of kidnapping [[Youngling|children]] to recruit into his [[Guattako's army|child]] [[army]].{{StoryCite|story=The Weapon|book=Age of Republic Special 1}} Some time before his reelection, Valorum witnessed{{Databank|twazzi|Twazzi}} the acrobatic skills of the [[Frenk]] [[Twazzi]], whose proficiency he praised.{{TCW|The Box}} ===Reelection and second term=== {{Quote|Valorum didn't ''win'' the election; he was merely ''allowed'' to win. The Senate's special-interest groups require a chancellor who can be easily entangled in bureaucratic doubletalk and arcane procedure. That is how loopholes are maintained and illegalities overlooked.|Sheev Palpatine, to Wilhuff Tarkin, after Finis Valorum's re-election as Supreme Chancellor|}} Towards the end of his chancellery, and against political expectations, Valorum was elected to a second term. According to Palpatine, who presented himself as an ally but—as Darth Sidious, the [[Dark Lord of the Sith|Dark Lord]] of the [[Sith]]—secretly plotted Valorum's downfall, Valorum was allowed to win by special interest groups who exploited legal loopholes, such as in Republic free trade laws, and needed a Chancellor who would become entangled in the governmental bureaucracies. Despite his [[Supreme Chancellor election, 36 BBY|reelection]], citizens on Coruscant began placing bets on whether Valorum would be able to serve a full term. It was at that time that Palpatine's name was whispered as a potential successor. Valorum's chancellery was further hampered when he attempted to investigate the events of a disastrous [[Eriadu Conference|trade summit]] on [[Eriadu]], but was stonewalled by Eriadu's [[Governor|planetary governor]], [[Wilhuff Tarkin]], at the request of Palpatine. Tarkin himself had been elected governor on Eriadu despite opposition from House Valorum, further weakening the Chancellor's position. All the same, surviving an assassination attempt during the Eriadu Conference granted Valorum a brief boost in popularity that allowed him to push through taxational legislation.''[[Rise of the Separatists]]'' Under [[Prop 31-814D]], the galaxy's [[Free Trade Zone]]s became liable to taxation.{{BustCollectionCite|58|Star Wars Universe}} In the final [[Standard month|months]] of Valorum's chancellery, work began on the millennial celebrations intended to mark the thousand-[[Standard year|year]] anniversary of the foundation of the Galactic Republic, which followed the [[Jedi-Sith War|last war]] between the Jedi and the Sith. Valorum and his team spent time exploring logo designs and artwork to commemorate the event, and the chancellor himself was intimately involved in the design process. Valorum rejected 250 different revisions for a [[Millennial Celebration Invitation|millennial invitation]] for a variety of reasons—such as the warmth of the design as well as its exclusivity—out of concern for his declining public image. He ultimately delegated the responsibility for the design to Senator Palpatine, who finalized a design that featured [[Sistros Nevet]], the ancient lawmaker who helped create the original constitution of the Republic after the fall of the Sith. The concept and layout were created by the [[artist]] [[Naveela Betuine]], while the final execution was done by [[Dashira Dobeq]].''[[Star Wars Propaganda: A History of Persuasive Art in the Galaxy]]'' Another issue during his chancellorship was the [[Selonian worker scandal]]. As [[Senator]] [[Mon Mothma]] would later recall, the scandal dominated the attention of the Galactic Senate, pushing aside discussions such as the plight of the [[Alvadorjian]]s of [[Ylagia]].''[[Reign of the Empire: The Mask of Fear]]'' ===Political downfall=== ====Under siege==== {{Quote|Okay, we'll top the newscast with a report of ''Chancellor Valorum'' under ''siege'' from ''multiple'' crises—cut to the ''Trade Federation'' threatening ''blockades'' over the ''Republic's'' new taxes. And then cut to a voiceover about the ''Nautolans'' and the ''Anselmi'' on the verge of ''war'' over the theft of the ''Hope of Glee Anselm'' statue.|A [[Unidentified human producer|human producer]]|[[Jango Fett 4|''Jango Fett'' 4]]}} During Valorum's time in office, the Republic found itself in disagreement over the taxation of trade routes to outlying [[star system]]s. The [[Trade Federation]], which held a monopoly on shipping in the Outer Rim, was upset by the profits set to be lost to taxes under Prop 31-814D, which it had opposed after its proposal but failed to stop. Around [[33 BBY]],{{JangoFettSeriesDate}} talks between the Federation and Naboo delegates broke down, which was seen as an issue for Valorum.[[Jango Fett 1|''Jango Fett'' 1]] The Federation also began to threaten [[blockade]]s in response the new taxes it needed to pay, creating another crisis for Valorum. Overall, in fact, Valorum would find his administration suffering embarrassment after embarrassment by that time. Around the same time as the Federation's blockade threats, Valorum's administration attempted to put a stop to the ongoing [[Anselmi–Nautolan war|war]] between the [[Anselmi]] and [[Nautolan]] peoples of the planet [[Glee Anselm]]. Looking for a way to support a [[Anselmi–Nautolan treaty]] and prolong an uneasy peace between the two races, Valorum personally ordered the [[Republic Museum]] to release the invaluable [[Hope of Glee Anselm]] statue to both peoples, hoping a past symbol of Anselmi–Nautolan cooperation could begin a new era of peace. In a ceremony presided over by Republic [[Governor]] [[Tok]], who was secretly working to undermine the entire process as an [[agent]] of [[Count]] [[Dooku]], Tok unveiled the Hope of Glee Anselm, only for it to be quickly [[Heist of the Hope of Glee Anselm|stolen]] by a group of Nautolan extremists. Losing the statue was yet another embarrassment for Valorum, who offered no comment to the press when asked. In the end, the revelation that the Nautolan Ambassador [[Fiarok]] was behind the robbery shattered any hope of peace for Glee Anselm, although Fiarok himself claimed to have been set up. The failure of the peace effort was yet another major blow to Valorum, who sat alone in the dark of his office after learning the news. The incident was a victory for Dooku, who knew the conflict on Glee Anslem would further destabilize the Republic government. In secret, Dooku was working with Sidious to bring what he saw as peace and order to the galaxy by working against a corrupt government.{{TOTJ|The Sith Lord}} ====Blockade of Naboo==== In [[32 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' mere months after{{Twitter|ethanjsacks|status/1803540946010906725|[[Ethan Sacks]]|quote=months. Was going to write a "few" {{C|In response to: ""Months" or "a month". A timeliner needs to know 🤣"}}|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/h410n}} the major blow Valorum suffered with the Anselmi–Nautolan war, the Federation put forth its own Mid Rim trade route bill—which secretly had been written by Sidious—that was repeatedly voted down and then suddenly brought back up in the Senate, much to Valorum's annoyance.''[[Queen's Peril]]'' In retaliation to Prop 31-814D and hoping such an action would support its own bill, the Trade Federation blockaded the planet Naboo in an attempt to force the Senate into a resolution favorable to the Federation. The Naboo Crisis was secretly engineered by Palpatine in order to end Valorum's chancellery, and was partly hastened by the events of the trade summit on Eriadu. The blockade cut off essential supplies to Naboo, plunging the Republic into a political crisis that the Senate was unable to resolve. ====Pyke Syndicate mission==== [[File:Sifo-Dyas_holo.png|thumb|left|250px|Jedi Master Sifo-Dyas investigated the Pyke Syndicate at the behest of Supreme Chancellor Finis Valorum.]] Concurrent to the Naboo Crisis,''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' there was a crisis in the [[Pyke Syndicate]], a criminal organization dealing in [[spice]], that could have resulted in a full-scale crime war beneath Coruscant's surface. In order to stabilize the Pykes, who held almost complete control over raw spice used to create illicit drugs, the chancellor contacted [[Jedi Master]] [[Sifo-Dyas]], who had experience with the criminal underworld. Valorum did not, however, inform the [[Jedi High Council]] that he was [[Mission to Oba Diah (Sifo-Dyas)|sending]] his personal aide, [[Silman]], with Sifo-Dyas to the Pyke [[planet]] of [[Oba Diah]]; the Senate feared that holding open discussions with the Pykes could legitimize their criminal activities and offer opposition leaders in the bureaucracy an opportunity to take down his administration.{{TCW|The Lost One}} After arriving on Oba Diah, Sifo-Dyas was diverted to [[Felucia]] by the Jedi Council, who ordered him to deal with a conflict between Felucian tribes. As Silman and the Jedi Master were leaving the planet, the Pykes—who had been hired by the [[Sith Lord]] [[Darth]] [[Dooku|Tyranus]]—shot [[775519|Sifo-Dyas‘s ship]] down, [[Death|killing]] the Jedi and taking Silman as a [[prisoner]]. Valorum and the Jedi were left believing that the pair had both been killed on Felucia. ====Naboo intrigue==== {{Quote|I will ''not'' defer. I have come before you to resolve this attack on our sovereignty now! I was not elected to watch my people suffer and die while you discuss this invasion in a committee. If this body is not capable of action, I suggest new leadership is needed. I move for a Vote of No Confidence in Chancellor Valorum's leadership."
"Now they will elect a new Chancellor, a strong Chancellor. One who will not let our tragedy continue.|Padmé Amidala and Sheev Palpatine|}} [[File:Amidala_arrives_on_Coruscant.png|thumb|right|250px|Queen Padmé Amidala journeyed to Coruscant beseeching Chancellor Valorum to liberate Naboo from the Trade Federation.]] To resolve the blockade of Naboo, Valorum sent Jedi Master [[Qui-Gon Jinn]] and his Padawan, [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]], to negotiate with [[Nute Gunray]], the [[Viceroy of the Trade Federation]]. The Federation [[Escape from the Saak'ak|attempted]] to kill the two Jedi and started an [[Invasion of Naboo|invasion]] of the planet shortly thereafter. [[Queen]] [[Padmé Amidala Naberrie|Padmé Amidala]] of Naboo escaped the planet with the help of the Jedi and traveled to Coruscant, seeking the help of Chancellor Valorum and the Senate. Valorum called for a special Senate session so Amidala could plead her case. The Senate session, which Valorum presided over, proved unproductive for Amidala's cause. Senator Palpatine and Queen Amidala proclaimed that the Federation had invaded Naboo, a claim that [[Lott Dod]], the Senator from the Trade Federation, disputed on the basis that no proof had been provided. Dod recommended to the Chancellor that the Senate appoint a commission to study the allegations, a recommendation that was seconded by the representatives of the planet [[Malastare]]. Valorum consulted with his advisors, including [[Vice Chair]] [[Mas Amedda]], and ultimately asked Amidala whether she would accept a commission. Amidala refused and, at Palpatine's urging, called for a [[Vote of No Confidence]] in Valorum's leadership. Unknown to Valorum was that Amedda was secretly working for Palpatine, and he knew that Valorum's indecision would make him look weak and present an opportunity to oust him from office. [[File:ZodKneelsBeforeAmidala-TPMHD.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Valorum was left stunned that Amidala called for a Vote of No Confidence against him.]] Amidala's motion led to Valorum's removal from office. A new [[Supreme Chancellor election, 32 BBY|election]] was called to replace him, and led to the nominations of Senator Palpatine, [[Bail Antilles]] of [[Alderaan]], and [[Ainlee Teem]] of Malastare. As Palpatine had predicted, the Invasion of Naboo created a sympathy vote in the Senate, and he was elected Supreme Chancellor in Valorum's place. Due to Valorum and the Senate's inability to act, Queen Amidala also returned to her planet and, with the help of the Jedi that Valorum had first sent to Naboo, ended the invasion. ===Post-chancellorship=== {{Quote|It's been a long time, my friend.|Finis Valorum, to Yoda, during the Clone Wars|}} Valorum's political fall and the liberation of Naboo led to changes within the shipping conglomerates. The Trade Federation's monopoly on the Outer Rim was broken, and [[Valorum Shipping]], controlled by House Valorum, suffered a loss of prestige. As a result, other companies, such as [[Eriadu Mining and Shipping]], found new prosperity. [[File:Valorum_Yoda_The_Lost_One.png|thumb|right|250px|During the Clone Wars, Grand Master Yoda visited Valorum as part of an investigation in the death of Sifo-Dyas.]] Valorum maintained an estate on Coruscant for several years after his chancellorship. During the [[Clone Wars]], which were partly precipitated by the Naboo Crisis and which were also engineered by Chancellor Palpatine,{{Film|II}} the Jedi found a [[lightsaber]] that had once belonged to Sifo-Dyas, who the Jedi had previously learned was the one who secretly commissioned the creation of the [[clone trooper]]s comprising the ranks of the [[Grand Army of the Republic]]. The Jedi began investigating Sifo-Dyas' disappearance, which led to the uncovering of a file sealed by Valorum's administration regarding the events on Oba Diah. [[Yoda]], the [[Grand Master]] of the [[Jedi Order]] and an old friend of the former Chancellor's, met with Valorum at Valorum's estate on Coruscant. At Yoda's request, the ex-Chancellor recounted the events that led to the mission on Oba Diah. Valorum's information [[Mission to Oba Diah (Clone Wars)|led]] Obi-Wan Kenobi and [[Anakin Skywalker]] to Oba Diah, where they discovered that Silman was still alive—though he was soon killed by Count Dooku—and that the Sith had helped orchestrate the creation of the [[Cloning|clone]] army. ===Legacy=== {{Quote|Had the Senate chosen a different chancellor after the deposition of the weak, ineffectual Valorum, galactic order itself might have fallen apart.|Part of the docent of the Emperor's Museum|''[[Leia, Princess of Alderaan]]''}} Thirteen years after he conspired to remove Valorum from office in order to seize power for himself, Palpatine [[Order 66|ordered]] the [[Great Jedi Purge|systematic genocide]] of the Jedi by the clone armies, [[Proclamation of the New Order|reorganized]] the Republic into the [[Galactic Empire]], and declared himself [[Galactic Emperor]].{{Film|III}} Despite Valorum's reputation as an ineffective leader, some [[Coruscanti]] citizens had fond memories of the former Supreme Chancellor and gossiped about him, particularly after Emperor Palpatine all but removed himself from public life. In [[5 BBY]],{{AndorDate|107}} Valorum's name was spoken among the murmur of voices at multiple dinner parties held by [[Chandrilan]] senator [[Mon Mothma]].{{Andor|Announcement}} {{Andor|Narkina 5 (episode)}} By [[3 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' places [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa's]] birth in [[19 BBY]]. The events of ''[[Leia, Princess of Alderaan]]'' commence just after Organa's sixteenth [[birthday]], which places the events of the novel in 3 BBY. the [[Emperor's Museum]] on Coruscant remembered the former Chancellor as a "weak, ineffectual" leader who had done little to improve the state of the Republic. ==Personality and traits== ===Overview=== {{Quote|Chancellor Valorum seems to think there is hope.|Padmé Amidala, to Sheev Palpatine|}} [[File:FinisValorum-TPM.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Finis Valorum was a well-meaning civil servant whose chancellorship became mired in baseless accusations of corruption.]] Valorum was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] who stood at 1.7 [[meter]]s (5 [[foot|feet]], 7 inches). By his chancellorship, he had [[Color|white]] hair, blue eyes, and fair skin. For his entire life, Valorum prepared for when he could one day become the Supreme Chancellor. Once elected, he enjoyed the privileges that came with being the leader of the Republic, though this attitude was to his detriment as ordinary voters did not respond well to it. Despite this, while his administration was hampered by corruption and the complex bureaucracies of the Republic, as Supreme Chancellor he was nonetheless a well-meaning man and a progressive diplomat.{{SWCT|set=Base Series 1|cardname=Chancellor Valorum - Galactic Republic}} Valorum was reelected several times, and celebrated each time by redecorating his office, changing the color scheme of his surroundings.''[[The Living Force]]'' The final days of his term saw him attempt to resolve the conflict between the Trade Federation and Naboo, but his efforts led to his removal from office. ===Political opinions=== Valorum held a low opinion of senators who represented companies instead of worlds; however, such an opinion was old fashioned by the time he was Chancellor, resulting in him keeping it private. In fact, he worked to ensure he did not showcase bias towards either type of senator. For all of his private beliefs and progressive tendencies as a diplomat, Valorum bound himself to the Republic's bureaucratic system, even when it was exploited by corporations, and often put up little to no fight against the rigid complex within which he worked, something that played a major role in his removal from office because it was pointed out to Amidala by Palpatine. Palpatine believed that Valorum did not care about the [[Coruscant Underworld|lower levels]] of Coruscant, beneath its surface, and suggested that he was happy to pretend they did not exist.[[Obi-Wan and Anakin 2|''Obi-Wan and Anakin'' 2]] All the same, when Valorum believed he needed to act to prevent an underground war from breaking out on Coruscant during his chancellery, he elected to dispatch Sifo-Dyas to Oba Diah to speak with the Pyke Syndicate, demonstrating a willingness to negotiate with criminal elements despite knowing such a move could be controversial. To ensure the Pykes were not granted legitimacy from these talks and that his political opposition was not granted new ammunition, Valorum believed the entire operation needed to be kept secret, even hiding its details from the Jedi Council. ==Skills and abilities== {{Quote|Enter the bureaucrats, the true rulers of the Republic—and on the payroll of the Trade Federation, I might add. This is where Chancellor Valorum's strength will disappear.|Sheev Palpatine, to Padmé Amidala|}} Though well-intentioned in his approach to governance, Valorum was nonetheless unable to rein in the complex and powerful bureaucracies that the Senate had become entangled in. According to Palpatine, Valorum's reelection was achieved only through the desires of the special interests, who wanted a Chancellor who would be unable to push back on their power and influence. Despite being unable to control them, he was aware of them and could at times counter them. When he assigned Sifo-Dyas to deal with the conflict in the Pyke Syndicate, Valorum and the Senate committee in charge of the situation feared that open negotiations with the Pykes could legitimize the Syndicate's criminal enterprise, as well as strengthen opposition leaders in the bureaucracy. As a result, they chose to keep their discussions with the Pykes a secret. The end of Valorum's chancellery was marked by inaction over the Naboo Crisis, as Valorum deferred to the interests of the Trade Federation, despite wanting to help Naboo during the invasion. His inability to control the bureaucracies allowed Palpatine to exploit Valorum's political weaknesses, which led to Valorum's removal from office as well as the [[Supreme Chancellor election, 32 BBY|election]] for Palpatine as the new Chancellor. ==Equipment== Valorum wore an ornate blue [[velvet]] [[Overcloak/Canon|overcloak]].''[[Star Wars: The Visual Encyclopedia]]'' ==Behind the scenes== {{Quote|I said, 'What's he like, the president of the universe?' And George Lucas said, 'He's a good man but he's beleaguered—a bit like [Bill] Clinton.' That was before Clinton was as beleaguered as he is now, of course.|Terence Stamp, in a 1998 interview with ''Star Wars Insider''|{{InsiderCite|41|Terence Stamp: Stamp of Approval}}}} Supreme Chancellor Valorum first appeared in [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], where he was played by [[Terence Stamp]]. Stamp, who filmed all of Valorum's scenes against a blue screen, took the role of Valorum because he felt that the character was not a one-dimensional cameo, and he wanted to work with [[George Lucas]], the creator of ''[[Star Wars]]'' and the writer and director of ''The Phantom Menace''. Stamp did not have much time to prepare for the role and was unable to read the full script, so he felt he did not have much to base his character on. To understand what Valorum was like, Lucas told Stamp that Valorum was similar to then-[[Wikipedia:President of the United States|United States President]] [[Wikipedia:Bill Clinton|Bill Clinton]], describing Valorum as "a good man but he's beleaguered," though Stamp noted that this was prior to Clinton's impeachment trial. Stamp later expressed disappointment in the role and how it was filmed—despite appearing in scenes with [[Natalie Portman]], the two never acted together on set.{{WebCite|url=http://www.theforce.net/episode2/story/Terence_Stamp_says_no_Episode_II_for_him_75812.asp|text=Terence Stamp says no Episode II for him|author=Scott Chitwood|date=2000-07-18|archivedate=20160413075042}} [[File:Valorum_TCW_Concept_Art.png|thumb|right|250px|Kilian Plunkett designed Valorum's animated appearance for "The Lost One."]] The character returned for a second [[canon]] appearance in "[[The Lost One]]," the tenth episode of [[The Clone Wars: The Lost Missions|The Lost Missions]], the sixth and penultimate season of the animated television series ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]''. For the animated appearance, the character was designed by ''The Clone Wars'' artist [[Kilian Plunkett]]{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/the-lost-one-episode-guide|text="The Lost One" Episode Guide | The Clone Wars}} and voiced by [[Ian Ruskin]]. The character's full name of Finis Valorum, which was not used in ''The Phantom Menace'' or "The Lost One," was used in [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]],''[[Star Wars: Episode I: The Visual Dictionary]]'' including stories such as Luceno's [[2001]] novel ''[[Cloak of Deception]]'';''[[Cloak of Deception]]'' the name was introduced into official canon in the [[2014]] mobile app ''[[Star Wars Journeys: The Phantom Menace]]''''[[Star Wars Journeys: The Phantom Menace]]'' as well as the novel [[Tarkin (novel)|''Tarkin'']], by [[James Luceno]]. The name "Valorum" has been part of ''Star Wars'' since the earliest drafts of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']]. In [[The Star Wars rough draft|''The Star Wars: Rough Draft'']], [[Valorum (The Star Wars)|Valorum]] was a [[Knights of Sith|Knight of Sith]] who was demoted to the level of stormtrooper after failing to capture Rebel fighters, before defecting from the Galactic Empire and joining the Rebels;[[The Star Wars rough draft|''The Star Wars'' rough draft]] the character bore some similarities to Darth Vader.{{DB|character|finisvalorum|Valorum, Supreme Chancellor Finis}} For [[The Star Wars first draft|''The Star Wars: First Draft'']], the character was renamed Dodana.[[The Star Wars first draft|''The Star Wars'' first draft]] The name Valorum was again used in a later draft, titled ''[[Adventures of the Starkiller, Episode I: The Star Wars]]''. Although he did not physically appear in the story, Prince [[Espaa Valorum]] was the Master of the Sith. Darth Vader served as his second in command.''[[Adventures of the Starkiller, Episode I: The Star Wars]]'' A discrepancy about Valorum arose after the publication of ''[[Star Wars Character Encyclopedia: Updated and Expanded]]'' in [[2016]]. The [[Databank (2014-)|Databank]] on [[StarWars.com]] lists Valorum's height as 1.83 meters, while ''Star Wars Character Encyclopedia: Updated and Expanded'' lists it as 1.7 meters. ==Appearances==
